description: Constitution §0.45 The "-First" Doctrine — the ONE canonical declaration of KYE's build-order primacy law. CEO directive (2026-07-12): the entire KYE ecosystem must be agentic-first, api-first, ai-first, schema-first, machine-readable-first, callable-first, discoverable-by-agents-first, dictionary-first, manifest-first, cloudflare-first, stripe-first, entity-first, registry-first, governed-and-governable-first — all constitutional principles. §0.45 UNIFIES them (§0.10 graft, the §0.42/§0.44 pattern) into ONE ordered doctrine, NOT fourteen parallel clauses (which would be §0 + §0.10). At design time the canonical artefacts land FIRST, in order — schema -> dictionary -> registry -> manifest -> OpenAPI (api-first) — before the code that consumes them; and every artefact is agentic-first, callable-first, discoverable-by-agents-first, machine-readable-first, entity-first, cloudflare-first, stripe-first, and governed-and-governable-first. Every primitive binds the EXISTING chapter it projects + the EXISTING enforcing gate that already makes 'code without its canonical-first artefact' mechanically fail. Only api-first and the ordering framing are genuinely NEW named contributions; all other primitives are explicit graft-citations. Enforced by scripts/gates/first-doctrine-canonical.mjs. EXTENDED 2026-09-08 (CEO directive, thirty-five '-first' primitives named in one message: NAMESPACE-FIRST leads): namespace-first is build-order step 1 — the ID class, schema family or package registry an identifier lives in is declared before anything is named inside it; every primitive now records the ONE canonical root that owns its concept (`root`, resolved through canonical-paths) or declares the measured gap on the row (`root_gap`, §0.62(c)); decoupled-first (external systems are governed SUBJECTS, never hard-coded dependencies of the entity / estate / ledger) and bidirectional-first (the entity / estate / ledger never assumes communication is only inbound) are grafted onto §0.61 · §0.47 · §51 · §75 · §38 · §48. Still ONE ordered doctrine, not forty-three siloes. GRAFTED 2026-11-19 (owner: 'kye must be plane first, diff first, context aware/first as constitutional principles at t0', then runtime · workspace · steps · hand-off · object first, 'x first must all be x as code', t0-first across every sub-processor, and illumination in conjunction with lineage): six rows (plane · context · diff · workspace · hand-off · runtime), two aliases on existing rows (object-first on entity-first, steps-first on workflow-first), one doctrine-wide invariant (x-as-code, doctrine_invariants), the t=0 scope of t0-first declared per sub-processor (t0_crossings), and the illumination observer bound to the lineage stream on the lineage-first row.

publication_rule.rationale: The doctrine (§0.45) is public; this map's enforcer wiring (which internal gate enforces each primitive) is operational self-governance metadata, kept internal like the §0.44 assurance-plane and §0.43 enforcer-scopes registries.

primitives.question: Does every governed thing — an action, a component, a credential, an evidence stream — name the ONE governance plane it belongs to, from a vocabulary declared before the thing exists, so that which plane it is on is answered by a field and never inferred from where a file sits?
primitives.grafts: §0.37 dev-plane interaction classes + §31 data_use plane + §12 / §61 / §68 rights planes + §69 Control-Plane MCP + §20 Analytics Plane + the plane category of kye:dictionary:action-classes (held byte-equal to kye.action_class.v1 by action-class-canonical since 2026-09-08) + owner 2026-11-19 (plane-first at t=0)
primitives.note: Identity-group primitive, after entity-first: a thing's identity, then the one plane it lives on. The root is the plane category of the action-classes dictionary: eleven terms (dev · data · user · commerce · agent · legal · clinical · physical · governance · employment · benefits). It is the only plane vocabulary that claims to own the governance planes and the only one with an enforcer; its own description still says nine planes. What the bound gate enforces TODAY: action-class-canonical validates every row of the action-class registry (166 rows on 2026-11-19) against kye.action_class.v1, where plane is required and takes one value, and holds the schema's plane enum byte-equal to the dictionary's plane terms. So every ACTION resolves to exactly one declared plane. DECLARED GAP (measured 2026-11-19 by reading every schema property named plane under the schema tree and counting its values in the registries that carry it): the word names at least six different axes with disjoint vocabularies. (1) Governance plane: kye.action_class.v1, 11 terms, the root. (2) Functional plane on implementation concepts: kye.implementation_registry.v1, 15 terms; its dictionary rows read 'observed value of plane', so the vocabulary follows the data. (3) Entity-type axis plane: kye.entity_type_registry.v1, 7 terms (data · policy · runtime · surface · evidence · identity · structural). (4) The §33 IP/OSS line: private · public · hybrid, on the admission matrix, the coordinate index and kye.evidence.pack.v1 coordinate.plane. (5) The lineage planes: build · runtime, kye.lineage.v1. (6) The enforcer-axis plane: repo · live-estate, on the generated enforcer axes. The constitution's control plane, data plane, dev plane and analytics plane are a seventh usage with no field behind them. Components (kye:registry:component-readiness), credentials (kye:registry:secrets) and evidence streams (kye:registry:lineage-sources) carry no governance-plane field, so the invariant holds for actions only. Owed, contract-first: keep this dictionary as the one root for the word plane; rename the five other axes to names that do not collide, each with collision_reviewed recorded (the namespace rule for ID-class terms applied to field names); then a plane field on component, credential and stream rows whose enum is a projection of this root, asserted the way action-class-canonical asserts it for actions. The renames move fields that admission-control, the coordinate index and the evidence-pack contract read, so choosing the names is an owner decision and is not part of this graft.

primitives.question: Is the isolated unit inside which work happens — an agent worktree, a CI runner, a session container, a sandbox, a staging or production surface, a tenant's workspace — DECLARED as a governed environment before any work starts in it, so isolation is a declared and decided property and never an arrangement someone made by hand?
primitives.grafts: §0.11 Zero Contamination (every parallel sub-agent runs isolated; every tenant-scoped query carries its trust-domain predicate) + §0.37 environment classes (isolated is not ungoverned) + §0.30 governed labs + kye.entity.workspace.v1 (an environment or dataspace owned by a Tenant) + owner 2026-11-19 (workspace-first)
primitives.note: Boundary-group primitive, first in the group: the inside must be declared before anything can cross out of it. The root declares six environment classes (agent-worktree · ci-runner · remote-container · sandbox-surface · staging-surface · production-surface), each a citizen with a pre-finality governor. What the bound gates enforce TODAY: total-citizenship-canonical proves every environment class names a t0 governor that resolves on disk and is issued into the identity backbone; tenant-predicate-canonical scans every D1 query in the app and admin Pages Functions and refuses a query on a tenant-scoped table that does not carry the tenant predicate in the same statement (decreases-only on the legacy offenders, an annotated cross-tenant query exempt). The tenant's own workspace is the kye.entity.workspace.v1 contract. DECLARED GAP (measured 2026-11-19): declaring an environment class is not deciding a workspace instance — nothing decides the creation of a worktree or a container before work starts in it; the delegated agents of the session that adopted this row run in clones made by hand outside the repository, an isolation the estate does not record; the builder PEP's declared-write-scope rule applies only when KYE_AGENT_ID is set, which only the ralph loop sets, so an Agent-tool subagent's workspace has no declared scope; and a governed lab (§0.30: several governed agents, environments and workflows packaged together) has no environment-class term. The word workspace has two referents here, a dev-plane environment and a tenant's dataspace; this row names both and records the collision rather than merging them.

primitives.question: Is every decision taken under a NAMED, SEALED context — the inputs, rule bundle, model build and signal versions it was decided against — assembled from canon and recorded evidence rather than from a conversation, so the decision can be replayed and a decision whose context cannot be replayed is refused?
primitives.grafts: §13 Replay (kye.replay.context_seal.v1: without the seal a decision cannot be replayed) + §0.3 evidence family (kye.evidence.pack.v1 requires replay_seal_ref) + §12 purpose request + §52 task-start governance envelope (a delegated agent's declared scope and allow-list) + §63 Memory Authority (memory is authority-bearing state) + §48 session-resume signal ingest + the reasoning-review discipline (chat is evidence, not authority) + CLAUDE.md 2026-09-22 (a grant that lives only in a conversation does not exist at t=0) + owner 2026-11-19 (context aware / context-first at t=0)
primitives.note: Decision-group primitive, after deterministic-first and before t0-first: a verdict that is a pure function of its input is replayable only if that input is sealed, and the t=0 decision is then taken under the sealed context. The root is the replay context seal: model build hash, rule bundle hash, per-signal versions, wall clock and RNG seed. What the bound gates enforce TODAY: kye.evidence.pack.v1 requires replay_seal_ref, and evidence-pack-standalone-canonical boots the reference evidence pack and proves its decision map, inputs and replay seal resolve from the file alone; self-governance-coverage refuses a watched privileged runtime path (rules gateway, decision engine, evidence engine and four more) whose source names none of decision_map, context_seal or evidence pack — it requires one of the three, so a path that emits a pack without a seal passes; delegated-agent-binding-coverage holds the §52 governance, refusal, completion and exchange envelope contracts and the binding manifest's task patterns, which are a delegated agent's declared working context. primitives.question: Is every consequential change expressed as a DIFF against declared state — the exact before and after (base and head, superseded and promoted digest, from-state and to-state) — and decided against that diff BEFORE it is applied, never a whole-state overwrite whose effect nobody computed?

primitives.root_gap: No one contract names the diff a consequential change applies. Measured 2026-11-19 by reading the dev-plane ledger contract, the two transition contracts and the merge driver: the diff is carried in four shapes and none is declared the shared one. (1) A merge decision names head_sha and leaves the base implicit: merge-authority accepts the PR head or its first parent (merge_subject of kye.devplane_action_ledger.v1). (2) A promotion names artefact_digest and, except for a component's first promotion, supersedes_digest (promotion_subject): the one shape that states both before and after. (3) A runtime state change is an edge from → to in TWO contracts, kye.state.transition.v1 (the State Engine) and kye.lifecycle_transitions.v1 (the lifecycle registry). (4) A schema rename is a row of kye.schema_migration_map.v1. Whole-state overwrites still exist and are recorded in CLAUDE.md: the merge=kye-derived driver writes one side of a file wholesale on the promise that a regeneration replaces it, and it dropped hand-written rows on forward merges (2026-08-22, 2026-09-04, 2026-09-06). Owed, contract-first: dictionary terms for the diff shapes → a before/after pair (base_ref and head_ref, or from_digest and to_digest) required on every pending_subject of the dev-plane ledger and on every lifecycle transition, with the two transition contracts reconciled to one → a reader that refuses a decision whose subject states only one side.
primitives.note: Decision-group primitive, after t0-first: t0-first says the decision comes before the act; diff-first says what the decision is taken against — the change, not the resulting state. What the bound gates enforce TODAY, each for one shape: merge-authority, a required status check, refuses a merge unless the latest ledger row names the PR head or its first parent, so the decision covers exactly the content that lands; devplane-t0-enforced verifies every recorded promotion row (digest and superseded digest) through the module the door writes with; workflow-governance-coverage holds every Worker deploy step to a decide phase, run before the step, against the promotion of that component's closure digest; lifecycle-state-canonical boots every declared machine and fires a transition, so a state change is a declared from → to edge. None of them asserts that a change is computed and decided as a diff in general; that is the declared root gap.

primitives.question: Does every mutable resource refuse a write unless the caller satisfies the resource's DECLARED concurrency policy at t=0 — one current writer under a time-bounded, fenced lease (or a matching state hash for optimistic writers), unlimited authorised readers, every lock attributable, every override evidenced, every stale writer rejected?

primitives.root_gap: No canonical root owns write-concurrency yet: kye.lease.v1 is the admission lease (a decision bounded in time) and carries no resource, holder, mode or fencing token; no dictionary declares lock modes; no registry declares a concurrency policy per resource class; nothing declares a fencing token, an ETag / If-Match or a 423 response (measured 2026-09-08 across the specs, the constitution and the runtime). Owed, contract-first (task #89): the lock-mode dictionary → the kye.lease.v1 extension (resource · holder · mode · fencing_token · session fingerprint) → one concurrency-policy registry (rows per resource class and sector pack: mode · lease TTL · override authority · fingerprint policy) → the lock action classes (acquire · renew · release · force-release · transfer) → the lock.* event family → the Lock Rail as one §40 concept on a per-resource Durable Object → the lease + fence check as one step of the existing PEP. The three gates bound here enforce the t=0, real-engine and WORM properties every lock event must already satisfy; the concurrency check itself is not yet enforced.
primitives.note: Decision-group primitive. lock-first and lease-first FOLD here (one concept, two mechanisms — three rows would be the parallel-doctrine explosion §0.45 forbids). Pessimistic (exclusive lease, humans and long workflows) and optimistic (state_hash / If-Match → 409, agents and APIs) are two admissible policies of ONE primitive. A fencing token is issued by the resource's single-writer Durable Object, monotonic per resource, and travels INTO the ledger commit so replay can prove the write was fenced. Cerbos and any other policy engine remain a PORT into the KYE PDP (policy-engine-adapter-canonical), never the deciding step above the lock rail.

What the bound gates enforce TODAY: cascade-coverage proves the build-plane graph covers the artefacts it claims; admission-control admits the registry and its stream rows against their contract and reads each row's ephemeral flag through the shared path probe; universal-bindings-canonical proves no artefact stands without a typed edge. DECLARED GAP (measured 2026-11-18): no gate asserts the resolver's ANSWER (no gate reads kye.lineage or the sources registry by name); all three runtime streams are ephemeral, untracked files, so a lineage answer here is a fact about which runs happened on one machine; the committed dev-plane action ledger is not declared as a stream; there is no commit → build → artefact digest → live version edge, so a deployed artefact cannot be traced to its source; and production WORM streams are not queried. The illumination engine is the §0.52 illumination observer — kye:observer:illumination, row 'illumination' of kye:registry:observers — implemented by scripts/build-coordinate-index.mjs through scripts/lib/coordinates.mjs and writing the coordinate index; kye.counterparty_handshake.v1 names it as what a counterparty uses to LOCATE and re-derive a proof from its EvidenceCoordinate. Bound here by declaration: illumination reads the lineage stream as its source — one stream, many projections (§0.10, §0.62) — the build plane being the §53 cascade graph both already read, and the runtime plane being the streams this row's root declares. ladder_groups.meaning: what a thing IS before it is shaped
the artefacts that declare it, in landing order
the external law it binds to, stated honestly
how it crosses, both ways, owned one way
how authority is exercised over it
how it moves through the estate
how it is seen and consumed
the platform bindings it runs on

ladder_note: LOCKED ORDER (2026-09-08, CEO: 'order at your complete discretion — lock what is needed / must have / essential / fundamental'; the CEO's own sequence of the same day was a sample of thinking aloud). Ten groups, each answering one question in the order the questions must be answered: IDENTITY (what a thing is: namespace · entity) → CANON (the artefacts that declare it, in landing order: canonical · vocabulary · dictionary · schema · contract · registry · manifest · api) → REGIME (the external law it binds to, stated honestly under §70: jurisdiction · regulatory · framework · standards · compliance) → BOUNDARY (how it crosses, both ways, owned one way: decoupled · bidirectional · event · gateway · multi-x · cross-x-governed) → DECISION (how authority is exercised over it: policy · invariant · deterministic · t0 · concurrency · governed-and-governable · enforcer) → FLOW (how it moves: rail · workflow · pipeline · promotion · lifecycle) → RECORD (what remains at emission: evidence · lineage · audit · worm · reporting) → FINALITY (how a fact becomes final: clearing · reconciliation · resolution · settlement) → PROJECTION (how it is seen and consumed: graph · topology · query · machine-readable · discoverable · callable · agentic · reverse-marketplace) → SUBSTRATE (cloudflare · stripe). Two deliberate departures from the sample: the dictionary lands before the schema (a schema enum is a projection of dictionary terms, asserted byte-equal by action-class-canonical — the 2026-09-08 `benefits` plane finding), and clearing precedes reconciliation → resolution → settlement (clearing is admissibility BEFORE the act; the other three are the post-observation order). Governing principle of the boundary group: BIDIRECTIONAL COMMUNICATION, UNIDIRECTIONAL AUTHORITY — every fact has exactly one authoritative source and one conflict rule; an observation never mutates canonical state; transport is governed at t=0 through an atomic ledger commit over state + outbound event (outbox → queue → connector worker). A declared timeout (kye.agent.workflow.v1 step.timeout_ms) is the one wait contract, reused by the finality lane for 'confirmation never arrived'. Essentiality: fundamental = identity · canon · regime · boundary · decision · record · finality; structural = flow · projection; substrate = cloudflare · stripe. GRAFTED 2026-11-18 (owner: relationship topologies, multi-x and cross-x first class and canonical, contract-first at t=0): multi-x-first and cross-x-governed-first close the boundary group in that order — plurality on every axis, then every crossing between the plural values governed — and topology-first follows graph-first in the projection group. The groups, their questions and the order of every prior primitive are unchanged; the three rows name roots that already existed (the plurality registry, the boundary registry, the relationships dictionary), so nothing was declared beside a canonical to make room for them. GRAFTED 2026-11-19 (owner 2026-11-18: promotion-first sandbox → production, lineage-first, reverse-marketplace-first): promotion-first follows pipeline-first in the flow group (a pipeline derives an artefact, a promotion moves it between environments); lineage-first follows evidence-first in the record group (evidence seals one decision, lineage joins records end to end); reverse-marketplace-first closes the projection group after agentic-first. Two name roots that already existed (the dev-plane action ledger, the lineage-sources registry) and declare their measured gaps on the row; the third declares that no root exists (root_gap) and records that masterblueprint §11 S-29 had classed it a strategy invariant. The groups, their questions and the order of every prior primitive are unchanged. GRAFTED 2026-11-19 (owner: plane first, diff first, context aware/first at t0; runtime, workspace, steps, hand-off and object first; every x-first as code): plane-first closes the identity group (a thing's identity, then its one plane); workspace-first opens the boundary group (the inside is declared before anything crosses out of it) and hand-off-first closes it (control handed across, after the crossing is governed); context-first follows deterministic-first and diff-first follows t0-first in the decision group (a verdict is replayable only under a sealed context, and the t=0 decision is taken against the change, not the resulting state); runtime-first follows promotion-first in the flow group (what runs after a promotion is the declared, canonical, booting implementation). steps-first and object-first are carried by workflow-first and entity-first as aliases. x-as-code is a doctrine-wide invariant (doctrine_invariants), not a rung. Relative order of every prior primitive is unchanged; absolute ranks were renumbered to stay contiguous.
